caption: Medical aid takes nearly a quarter of our pension. What does it take from yours?

slides.title:
How we live on
our R16 200
p/m pension
Living in Margate
slides.body:
Him 64, her 61
Married, own their house
Income: His pension R12 900 + her part-time work R3 300
Household income: R16 200 p/m

slides.title: Medical aid
slides.includes: Two people on a hospital plan, no savings account
slides.body: It's the biggest line and we both know it. Neither of us wants to be the one who drops it.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Two adults, the grandchildren on Sundays
slides.body: Sunday lunch costs more than a normal Tuesday. We'd do it again.

slides.title: Petrol & car
slides.body: The car is paid off. It's the only thing in this budget I enjoy owning.

slides.title: Rates & water
slides.body: The house is ours but the council still sends an invoice every month.

slides.title: Electricity
slides.body: He thinks the timer saves money. I haven't checked.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Funeral policies R480, Help for our son R1 000, Phone & TV R700, Medication co-payments R750, Church & stokvel R300
slides.body: Our son's R1 000 is supposed to be a loan. We both know how that goes.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R16 200. I worked for thirty years and now I'm doing this sum every month.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
My wife uploaded our statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted the transactions for us.

The medication co-payments were more than I would have guessed.

No bank login needed.
